author: British Museum
title: British Museum catalogue record for photograph Oc-A35-45

notes.text: This British Museum catalogue record describes a 1980 photograph by Katesa Schlosser. It is registered as a documentary source, not as a physical Rapa Nui artefact. The 30 September 2026 image-rights review found that the museum's image page explicitly says the image is unavailable for download and supplies no reusable image licence or credit, so no image is published. Its description places three named ahu sites in the frame. The description spells the third name as ‘Ahu Ko Te Riki’; the record's structured associated-place link identifies ‘Ahu Ko Te Riku’, which is used for the linked MoSA site identity while the claim preserves the description's wording. The museum's longer contextual comment is collapsed in the live record and was not extracted. The former site-targeted extraction is retained here after correcting the collection boundary: “view of three ahu's (ceremonial platforms) with moai (figure carvings), Ahu Vai Uri on the left” (Description) “Ahu Tahai in the centre” (Description) “Ahu Ko Te Riki on the right” (Description) The site is not a collection object because its displacement is not under investigation.
